oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Increasing Latinas' Full Potential in University Leadership Roles: Towards Liberated Leadership
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: Lizette A. Navarrete-Burks
Laura J. Link
Diane M. Miller
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Latina faculty play a central role in university settings, shaping our understanding of the factors that impact Latina leadership access and potential. This qualitative single-case study used a constructivist grounded theory approach to investigate how systems of power and exclusion shape the lived experiences of tenure-track Latina faculty in higher education leadership. Ten participants at one urban Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) in the south-central United States participated in open-ended interviews, which served as the sole data source for the study. During the data analysis, three themes emerged: (a) navigating institutional dynamics, (b) cultivating supportive networks, and (c) leveraging cultural capital. Findings show that institutions often undervalue and misunderstand the unique contributions that Latina faculty bring to leadership positions. Furthermore, Latinas in this study did not realize their full leadership potential; instead, they dedicated their efforts to navigating barriers. We share implications for higher education practice and policy and present a framework to help realize greater leadership potential.
